/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 18 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3370 (34)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5768 (112)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2251 (-31)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1767 (5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 988 (8)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the week on a firmer note, with the BCI 182 5TC increasing by $1,019 to $52,315. The C5 index gained 0.325 to $16.575, while the C3 increased by 0.291 to $42.955. In the Pacific, conditions remained steady throughout the day. The presence of two major miners helped underpin sentiment, while improving bid levels provided further encouragement. Early indications suggested business was concluded around $16.30, however, momentum built as the session progressed, with several fixtures ultimately reported in the $16.50-$16.55 range. The Atlantic remained firm despite a quieter trading session. Following yesterday's burst of activity, many market participants appeared content to take stock, resulting in fewer fresh fixtures being reported. Nevertheless, underlying sentiment stayed positive, with most C3 offers said to be positioned at $43.00 and above.
PANAMAX
The week closed with the P5TC falling a further $273 to finish at $20,262. Activity in the North Continent was reported to have eased compared with previous days, although brokers noted that the tonnage count remains relatively oversupplied. The US Gulf is beginning to contribute additional demand, however, sentiment remains negative across both trans-Atlantic and fronthaul routes for the time being. Market sources indicated that several participants with more forward positions have stepped back to assess current market fundamentals and await further direction next week. The Pacific is facing a similar situation to the Atlantic, with an excess of available tonnage outweighing the volume of cargoes in the market. Grain cargoes from the North Pacific were cited as a rare source of optimism, although Owners continue to revise their rate expectations closer to Charterers' bids in an effort to generate momentum and establish dialogue. Market participants have also reported a slowdown in prompt cargo requirements from Indonesia. At the same time, a growing number of owners are favouring shorter-duration trips to China, while longer-haul Australian and North Pacific routes continue to offer less attractive returns.
SUPRAMAX
The usual Friday of early activity petering out and a quiet afternoon prior to the weekend. The 11TC average saw another small increase of $57 to finish the week at $22,332, up $604 on the week. There was little reported in the Atlantic, which was a disappointment after the implied levels being discussed yesterday for scrap off the Continent. In Asia, NoPac continued to be very active with the Norse Stride (66,307 2025) prompt Lianyungang said to be on subjects via NoPac with potash to Indonesia at $24,500 to Pacific Basin (basis scrubber for Charterers benefit) and the Seabird (63,553 2016) CJK 15-16 September fixed a soda ash stem to the same area at $20,250, but the Charterer remained private. The Sophiana (61,620 2016) Onsan 23-25 September was also fixed via NoPac to South East Asia at $21,000, but there were no further details, and the Agios Nikolas (57,902 2014) Lianyungang 20-22 September went on subjects to Polaris at $20,000 for a trip via NoPac to Taiwan.
HANDYSIZE
Building on the week’s momentum, the market closed on a firm and positive note, with constructive sentiment prevailing across the Atlantic. The BHSI climbed to 988, while the 7TC average rose by $143 to close at $17,776. Conditions in the Continent and Mediterranean remained steady, while the US Gulf and South Atlantic maintained a firm tone following a strong week. The HG Liverpool (40,184 2025) open spot Callao was fixed by Cargill for a trip via Upriver to China at around $18,000. Elsewhere, the Paiwan Champion (39,785 2026) was fixed by Prudent for a trip from Recalada to South Africa at around $26,000–$27,000, although further details were not disclosed. The Nordic Malmoe (35,843 2012) was placed on subjects by Radius on voyage terms for a scrap trip from the US East Coast to the East Mediterranean, again with limited details available. In contrast, activity in Asia remained subdued, with few fixtures reported and rates holding around last-done levels.

Market Fundamentals
China Blast Furnace Activity

In the week to 18 September, Chinese blast furnace capacity utilisation fell 0.80 percentage points from the prior week to 82.3%, while daily molten iron output remained near flat at 2.4 Mt/day, MySteel data show. Only 7.8% of the 247 sampled mills are in profit, unchanged from the prior week and the lowest share since late-September 2024.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape had a quieter end to the week with most interest again centred on October and Q4. September garnered some interest, trading between 49000 – 50000. October opened firm trading 49250, before easing back to 48500 and trading within a relatively limited range the remainder of the day down to a low of 48250. November traded 46000 – 46750, while December traded between 43750 – 44100 and Q4 26 changed hands between 46000 – 46750. Q1 27 was active between 31900 and 32100, with several larger clips around 32000. Cal27 traded at 33500.

PMX
PMX was relatively quiet today compared to the rest of the week with most interest centred on October, November and Q4. September printed at 21,300. October traded from 22,100–22,200 early, firmed through the morning to 22,350–22,500, then settled back around 22,300–22,350 in the afternoon. November was steady around 22,500 early before firming to a high of 22700. December was active around 21,600–21,850. Q4 26 traded mainly around 22,200, later trading at 22,233. Q1 27 was concentrated at 18,150, while Cal 27 traded from 18,100 up to 18,200. Overall, the session had a firmer tone through the front months, with October and November providing most of the liquidity.

SMX + HANDY
A low volume day on SMX to end the week, as firmer levels held across the curve and trades remained in a narrow range. Oct traded within a tight range between 21700 – 21800, Nov traded 21550 – 21625, Dec 20800 – 20900, with the Q4 trading 21300 – 21500. Some trading on the back endm Q1 trading 16650 – 16700, Q2 at 16650, Q3 16600 – 16650 and Q4 16405 – 16650, while the cal27 traded 16600 – 16700.

NOPAC OPENED THE WEEK WITH A LENGTHY CARGO LIST AND CHARTERERS LOOKING TO COVER EARLY WERE FORCED TO STILL PAY HEALTHY LEVELS WITH AROUND MID $22'S BKI CJK REPORTED ON MONDAY EVEN WHILE CHARTERERS WITH MORE TIME ON THEIR HANDS WERE BIDDING AROUND $20K BKI. ELSEWHERE KAMSARMAXES WERE STILL ABLE TO SECURE STRONGER LEVELS IN THE $20'S FOR INDO/INDIA CARGOES. THE WEEK HAS ENDED ON THE USUAL QUIETER TONE WITH CARGO VOLUMES THINNING AS MOST CHARTERERS ARE NOW HAPPY TO WAIT UNTIL NEXT WEEK.
